subject: Deployment needs follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (SSO / KMS / Logging)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Lee <tom@fintechco.com>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & follow-ups — deployment constraints (SSO / KMS / logging)

Hi Tom / Sarah — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a couple of qualification questions so we can recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem).

Recap:
- You want to run Redwood for customer-facing features (chat + embeddings) with strict security and retention requirements.
- Primary concerns raised: SSO integration, customer-managed KMS/HSM, and long-term logging/retention for audit.

A few clarifying questions so we can map to the right offering:
1) SSO: Do you require IdP-initiated SSO with SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning, or is OAuth/OIDC acceptable? Any IdP vendor preference (Okta, Azure AD, Ping)?
2) KMS/HSM: Will you require a customer-managed KMS (CMK) where keys never leave your control (AWS KMS with CloudHSM backing or an HSM appliance)? Or is BYOK acceptable where keys are managed but backed by Redwood?
3) Logging/retention: What is your required retention for audit logs (days/years)? Any special archival/legal hold requirements?

What we typically see: Hosted API is fastest to get started but cannot meet customer-managed HSM requirements today. Dedicated capacity can often meet stricter networking and isolation needs and supports many KMS integration patterns, and Private (VPC/on-prem) is the path when customers require full control (HSM, custom KMS, long retention, private networking). Happy to map your answers to a recommendation and attach the right artifacts (SOC2 summary, Dedicated overview, Private checklist).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm answers to the 3 questions above.
- If you require CMK/HSM or 7+ year retention, we schedule a security deep-dive with our security lead + SE (30–60m).
- I’ll share our SOC2 summary and Dedicated vs Private one-pager.

Attaching: redwood-dedicated-overview.pdf (summary), redwood-private-vpc-checklist.docx (high level).

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & follow-ups — deployment constraints (SSO / KMS / logging)

Thanks Marissa — quick answers below.

1) SSO: Okta is our IdP. We require SAML 2.0 for admin UI access and SCIM for provisioning. OIDC might be used for internal apps but admin/console must be SAML.
2) KMS/HSM: We must use a customer-managed key that resides in our AWS account and is backed by CloudHSM. Keys cannot be exported. Essentially a strict BYOK/CMK requirement.
3) Logging/retention: We have regulatory requirements for 7 years retention of certain audit logs and a capability to apply legal holds. Logs must be exportable to our Splunk/archival S3.

Given that, Hosted API won't work for those KMS/retention constraints. We are primarily evaluating Dedicated vs Private. Cost/implementation time matters — Dedicated is preferable if it can meet CMK + long-retention and SSO. If not, we'll need Private (VPC or on-prem).

Please loop in your security/infra folks. Procurement will want a checklist of what is supported vs requires Private deployment.

Thanks — Tom

Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 08:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & follow-ups — deployment constraints (SSO / KMS / logging)

Tom — perfect, thanks for the clarity. 

Summary mapping based on your answers:
- SSO (Okta SAML + SCIM): Supported on all deployment modes for admin/console access, though Private gives the most control for network-level IdP integrations. We can do SAML + SCIM in Hosted for many customers, but enterprise SSO with strict network controls is more commonly paired with Dedicated or Private.
- KMS/HSM (CMK in your AWS account + CloudHSM): This is a blocker for Hosted. Dedicated can often be configured to integrate with a customer KMS in the customer AWS account (via VPC peering / private networking + KMS grant patterns) but CloudHSM-backed keys typically require Private (VPC-hosted or on-prem) for the highest assurance (keys never leave your account and HSM appliances can be placed in your environment). We should treat this as a likely requirement for Private unless our infra team can validate a Dedicated design that meets CloudHSM-backed CMK guarantees.
- Logging/retention (7 years, legal hold, export to Splunk/S3): Private gives the most straightforward path (we can ship logs directly to your S3/Splunk). Dedicated can be configured to forward logs into your archival pipelines but may require additional retention/archival agreements. Hosted has fixed retention limits that will not meet 7 years.

Recommended next steps:
1) Schedule a 45m security deep-dive with our security lead (Naomi) and SE (Dylan) to validate whether a Dedicated topology can meet your CloudHSM-backed CMK requirement or if Private is required.
2) I’ll attach our SOC2_summary.pdf and a one-page matrix that highlights Supported vs Requires Private for the items you called out.
3) If Dedicated is viable, we’ll scope an initial POC window (4–6 weeks) and a proof checklist; if not, we’ll scope Private (timeline/cost differ).

Please confirm availability for a deep-dive — Naomi & Dylan, are you available next week (Mon/Tue preferred)?

Thanks — Marissa

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf

Immediate asks:

Target dates: aim to run the deep-dive on Tue, Jun 24 or Wed, Jun 25 (FinTechCo prefers early afternoons ET). Marissa — I’ll coordinate calendar invites once you confirm availability.
